stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Inside Microsoft’s big Copilot rethink
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is fundamentally rethinking its Copilot offering.
The new vision positions Copilot as the 'OS for work'.
The strategy involved an exclusive, high-level briefing with key enterprise customers.

stories.title: OpenAI’s new agent is a shot at Meta — but can it compete with free?
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: OpenAI unveiled 'Dots,' a new AI agent powered by GPT-6 Astra, aiming to challenge competitors.
The launch is positioned as a direct competitive move against Meta's successful Muse AI agent platform.
The announcement occurred at OpenAI's DevDay conference, signaling a major push in the AI agent space.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies such as transformers and safetensors, and is related to the deepseek_v3 family.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is used for text-generation tasks within the ML ecosystem.
Tags confirm its relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key ML/AI tags such as 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and evaluation of Meta's latest open-source LLM releases.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance based on the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon through updates to its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The optimized engine also results in reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Google’s new Guided Vision feature can help you read the fine print
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Google is rolling out 'Guided Vision' within Gemini Live on compatible Android devices.
The feature uses AI to provide real-time audio descriptions of what the user points their camera at.
Key use cases include reading small text and identifying surrounding objects.

stories.title: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: A federal judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits against Google concerning its AI Overviews feature.
The lawsuits, filed by Chegg and Penske Media Corporation, alleged Google was negatively impacting web traffic.
Judge Amit Mehta ruled in favor of Google, effectively dismissing the antitrust claims related to the AI search features.

stories.title: Sony brings AI graphics upscaling to the regular PS5
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Sony is introducing a new AI upscaling technology named Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) for the standard PS5.
The technology is described as a 'new performance tier of AI upscaling' resulting from Sony's Project Amethyst collaboration with AMD.
This update represents a significant push in console hardware capabilities leveraging AI for graphical fidelity.

stories.title: Hacks of 2 federal agencies in a month have spilled a bonanza of sensitive data
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Federal government cybersecurity has faced a significant downturn recently.
Multiple hacks targeting two different federal agencies occurred within a single month.
These security breaches resulted in the exposure of a substantial amount of sensitive data.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws' to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
The work proposes a novel, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping to understand how these two efficient scaling techniques interact.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws,' a novel framework to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
Suggests a new direction for efficient model scaling by combining the benefits of recurrent structures and sparse activation mechanisms.

stories.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
stories.author: Bradley Emi
bullet_points: A significant portion (27.5% to 31.1%) of real-world web text used for LLM pretraining is increasingly being generated by AI.
The study examines the impact of this 'wild' AI-generated text—which is unlabeled and comes from diverse models—on language model training.
The research addresses the critical, emerging question of how synthetic data contamination affects the quality and behavior of large language models.

stories.title: EvoDuet: Bilevel Co-Evolution of Web Searching and Task Solving for Scientific Discovery
stories.author: Dongyeop Kang
bullet_points: Introduces EvoDuet, a novel bi-level optimization method for scientific discovery.
Addresses the limitation of LLMs stalling when external knowledge is required during search/solving tasks.
Co-evolves solutions and search queries iteratively, using a retrieval gate to manage knowledge gaps.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws' to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
The work proposes a novel, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping to understand how these two efficient scaling techniques interact.

stories.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
stories.author: Bradley Emi
bullet_points: A significant portion (27.5% to 31.1%) of real-world web text is increasingly being generated by AI models.
This 'wild' AI-generated text is unlabeled and enters pretraining corpora, posing a novel challenge to LLM development.
The research investigates how this pervasive, real-world synthetic data impacts the training and performance of large language models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can answer questions with probabilistic outputs, covering yes/no, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces improved performance and expanded model compatibility.
The update leverages GGUF model support via llama.cpp integration.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine capabilities, particularly on Apple silicon, broadening hardware support.

stories.title: Steam Deck 2: Is AMD Gainsborough the chip Valve’s been waiting for?
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The Steam Deck is nearing the end of its lifecycle, fueling demand for a successor.
Valve has historically required a significant performance and efficiency leap for the Steam Deck 2.
There is emerging speculation that AMD's Gainsborough chip may be the breakthrough hardware Valve is anticipating.

stories.title: Can VR glasses save VR?
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Meta has released new VR glasses, signaling a potential shift in the VR hardware market.
The high price point ($1,299) is noted as a barrier to mass consumer adoption.
The device is described as a significant advancement, potentially changing the VR landscape.

stories.title: Judge dismisses Chegg and Penske antitrust lawsuits targeting Google AI search
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits filed by Chegg and Penske against Google regarding its AI search.
The court ruled that the implications of AI search, while acknowledged, do not constitute an antitrust violation.
This decision suggests current legal frameworks may not classify AI search changes as anti-competitive behavior.

stories.title: Memory executives expect RAM shortage to continue through 2028
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Memory executives project that the RAM shortage will persist until 2028.
Future memory prices (2027) are anticipated to be significantly higher than current (2026) levels.
The report indicates ongoing supply constraints within the memory market.

stories.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: The game Stratego, which relies on hidden information, previously stumped AI systems.
The breakthrough involved implementing a second neural network.
This new network was specifically designed to guess the identity of the hidden pieces.

stories.title: As US relations fray, Canada gets serious about its own launch industry
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Canada is increasing its focus on developing a domestic medium-lift launch capability.
The Canada Rocket Company is central to this renewed national effort in the space sector.
The development is occurring amidst a backdrop of shifting geopolitical relations involving the US.

stories.title: PS5 emulation is suddenly making big strides on PC
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: PS5 emulation is showing significant recent improvements on PC.
Specific titles like Astro Bot and Demon's Souls are now reportedly running well via emulation.
This indicates a notable advancement in the feasibility of console emulation outside of dedicated hardware.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: The research addresses the sensitivity of Large Language Models (LLMs) to irrelevant prompt features, even when using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
The study introduces 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test how LLM predictions change while keeping the core problem and answer intact.
The findings suggest that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding can effectively improve the reasoning accuracy of LLMs.

stories.title: ViTeX-Bench: Benchmarking High-Fidelity Video Scene Text Editing
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research introduces ViTeX-Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating high-fidelity video scene text editing.
The core problem addressed is the difficulty of performing precise local text edits in video while maintaining scene dynamics and motion.
This work extends image-based scene text editing techniques to the more complex domain of video generation and manipulation.

stories.title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization
stories.author: Dimitris N. Metaxas
bullet_points: Introduces 'Turbo Harness,' a new framework for optimizing AI agent harnesses.
Addresses a limitation in current methods where a single global harness is applied uniformly.
Allows for instance-adaptive harness optimization by reusing information from the initial optimization process.

stories.title: WorldAuditBench: Interactive 3D World Auditing with Multimodal Agents
stories.author: Shiyu Chang
bullet_points: Introduces WorldAuditBench, a framework for auditing interactive 3D simulated worlds.
Aims to automate the detection of anomalies (e.g., floating objects, inconsistent geometry) in 3D environments.
Leverages multimodal AI systems, specifically VLMs and VLAs, to perform complex 3D world auditing.

stories.title: Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Cogentic is a new multi-agent orchestration framework designed for automated proof discovery.
It addresses the limitations of single-shot large language models when tackling complex, open mathematical problems.
The system utilizes an iterative prove-verify loop to manage long-horizon reasoning and overcome technical obstructions.

stories.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space
stories.author: Michael R. Lyu
bullet_points: Introduces MatLoom, a new compact, layer-oriented language for text-to-material generation.
The system generates not just appearance, but also the underlying construction rules for materials.
It uses alpha-masked layers and shared spatial expressions to explicitly define dependencies between patterns, color, and PBR channels.

stories.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: DynaHarness addresses the gap between high-level semantic reasoning and low-level physical execution in robot control.
It introduces a dynamic physical harness that integrates these two components via a shared execution contract.
The system aims to improve long-horizon manipulation by providing better guidance from episode failures for self-evolution.

stories.title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
stories.author: Emmanuel Abbé
bullet_points: Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE) agents are advancing on leaderboards but face stagnation issues.
Current advanced MLE agents rely on complex 'harnesses' like multi-agent orchestrators and retrieval subagents.
There is a discussion point regarding the trade-off between elaborate harnesses and using more primitive but improved coding agents with direct execution access.

stories.title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
stories.author: Jiayun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in clinical AI: standard accuracy metrics fail with imbalanced clinical data.
Proposes optimizing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) using AUROC, a class-balance-invariant ranking metric.
Focuses on prompt optimization techniques to improve the clinical utility and ranking performance of MLLMs.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the sensitivity of Large Language Models (LLMs) to irrelevant prompt features, even when using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
Researchers introduce 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test how much LLM predictions vary when only task-relevant information is preserved.
The study proposes that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding can effectively improve the reasoning accuracy of LLMs.

stories.title: Removing Timing Shortcuts Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text
stories.author: Oiwi Parker Jones
bullet_points: The research challenges recent claims of significant improvements in non-invasive brain-to-text decoding.
The study suggests that reported gains might be artifacts of specific data processing techniques, such as fixed-length window segmentation.
Removing 'timing shortcuts' (implicit interval estimation) leads to reproducible results without relying on specific brain data patterns.

stories.title: Image Classifiers are Efficient Self-Supervised Video Representation Learners
stories.author: Abir Das
bullet_points: Introduces VideoMSN, a Masked Siamese Network framework for self-supervised spatio-temporal video representation learning.
Avoids heavy 3D architectures and reconstruction-based autoencoders, offering computational efficiency.
Repurposes standard image Vision Transformers by treating videos as 'super images' composed of sampled frames.

stories.title: Is Weight Tying Still Beneficial for Decoder-Only LLMs in Private Settings Under DP-SGD?
stories.author: Razane Tajeddine
bullet_points: Investigates the effect of weight tying (input/output embedding sharing) in decoder-only LLMs when trained using DP-SGD.
Addresses a gap in current research regarding the performance impact of weight tying specifically under differentially private fine-tuning.
Relevant to the growing industry need for privacy-preserving LLM training methods.

stories.title: Compression Footprints as Security Signals for Model-Poisoning Defense in Federated Learning
stories.author: William Eiers
bullet_points: Proposes using 'compression footprints' as a novel security signal in Federated Learning (FL).
Shifts focus from traditional update geometry analysis to analyzing how lossy compression distorts updates.
The method aims to differentiate between honest and model-poisoning attack-generated updates based on compression behavior.

stories.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: DynaHarness addresses the challenge of long-horizon robot manipulation by bridging the gap between high-level semantic reasoning and low-level physical execution.
The system utilizes pretrained robot policies as action priors to guide the learning process.
It introduces a 'dynamic physical harness' that manages coordination via a shared execution contract, improving guidance from episode failures.

stories.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer
stories.author: Gao Huang
bullet_points: Proposes 'Looped Diffusion Transformer' as an alternative scaling method for text-to-image models.
Increases computational depth by repeatedly running shared Transformer blocks within each denoising step, keeping parameters fixed.
Aims to enable iterative refinement of internal representations without relying on explicit reasoning tokens.

stories.title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
stories.author: Jiayun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in applying Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to clinical diagnosis: reliance on accuracy metrics in imbalanced datasets.
Proposes optimizing prompt design in MLLMs using AUROC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve) instead of simple accuracy, which is more clinically relevant.
Focuses on improving the ranking capability of MLLMs for better performance in real-world, class-imbalanced medical scenarios.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: Investigates the sensitivity of Large Language Models (LLMs) to task-irrelevant prompt features, even when using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
Introduces 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test how changes in prompts affect LLM reasoning while keeping the core problem intact.
Demonstrates that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding can effectively improve the reasoning accuracy of LLMs.

stories.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space
stories.author: Michael R. Lyu
bullet_points: Introduces MatLoom, a new compact, layer-oriented language for text-to-material generation.
The system generates not just appearance, but also the underlying construction rules for materials.
It uses pretrained language models and alpha-masked layers to explicitly define dependencies between patterns, color, and PBR channels.

stories.title: Linguistic Loopholes in LLM Unlearning: From a 174-Language Benchmark to Coverage-Aware Unlearning
stories.author: Abhay Yadav
bullet_points: Identifies a 'cross-lingual loophole' in LLM unlearning, where removing knowledge in one language doesn't guarantee removal in others.
Proposes 'language budgeted multilingual unlearning' as a scalable solution to avoid the impracticality of unlearning across all languages.
Addresses the trade-off between complete knowledge removal and preserving unrelated model capabilities.

stories.title: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
stories.author: Jing Yu Koh
bullet_points: Computer Use Agents (CUAs) are demonstrating impressive capabilities, sometimes surpassing human performance on complex tasks.
A major hurdle for CUA adoption is their current speed and operational cost.
The paper proposes 'cua-speedrun' to establish standardized, reproducible benchmarking for CUA speed.

stories.title: Comparison of techniques for fine-tuning open-weight models for entity extraction from radiology reports
stories.author: Hari Trivedi
bullet_points: The research compares fine-tuning an open-weight model (Gemma-3-12B) against proprietary models (like GPT-4o) for entity extraction from radiology reports.
The study addresses critical industry concerns regarding privacy, cost, and reproducibility associated with using closed, proprietary AI models in clinical settings.
The specific task evaluated is multi-label intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) acuity extraction from non-contrast head-CT reports.

stories.title: Show HN: Janus – Go binary that runs GGUF models via Vulkan on AMD/Intel/Nvidia
stories.author: Maverick617
bullet_points: Janus is a new Go binary designed to run GGUF models.
It leverages Vulkan for hardware acceleration across AMD, Intel, and Nvidia GPUs.
This represents an effort to improve local LLM inference performance and accessibility.
